headline: The law firm Ropes & Gray will let its lawyers count up to 100 hours of AI experimenting and training toward their yearly billing targets, Reuters reports.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a concrete workplace change at a large firm, but only the opening paragraph could be checked and other firms named by Reuters are unknown to us.
importance_line: Lawyers at a large firm can now spend work time learning AI without falling behind on billable hours, though we saw only the opening of Reuters' report and not which other firms do the same.
summary: Reuters reports that the law firm Ropes & Gray now lets its more than 1,000 associates and counsel count up to 100 hours of AI experimenting and training toward their annual billing requirements, as part of a firmwide AI training initiative.
notes: Reuters page blocked (401); opening paragraph read via TradingView. default_v1 MOD; main subject is work and the legal profession, so SOC.
